quickSummary: Electrophiles: electron-deficient Lewis acids (NO₂⁺, BF₃, :CCl₂). Nucleophiles: electron-rich Lewis bases (OH⁻, CN⁻, NH₃). Ambident nucleophiles attack via two different atoms (CN⁻, NO₂⁻). 4 reaction classes: Substitution, Addition, Elimination, Rearrangement.
summary: Master electrophile and nucleophile taxonomy, ambident nucleophile reactivity, and fundamental reaction classes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Electrophiles vs. Nucleophiles
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Electrophiles vs. Nucleophiles

summaryBox.title: Reagent Classes
summaryBox.takeaway: Electrophiles = electron-pair acceptors (Lewis acids). Nucleophiles = electron-pair donors (Lewis bases). Ambident nucleophiles attack from 2 sites.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
REAGENT TAXONOMY
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  ELECTROPHILES (E⁺)                                      NUCLEOPHILES (Nu⁻)
  ├── Electron-pair ACCEPTORS (Lewis Acids)               ├── Electron-pair DONORS (Lewis Bases)
  ├── Positively charged or neutral with vacant orbitals  ├── Negatively charged or neutral with lone pairs
  └── Examples: H⁺, NO₂⁺, Cl⁺, BF₃, AlCl₃, SO₃, :CH₂      └── Examples: OH⁻, CN⁻, H₂O, NH₃, R-MgX
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Electrophiles ($\text{E}^+$)**: Electron-deficient species that accept electron pairs (Lewis acids). Include cations ($\text{NO}_2^+, \text{Cl}^+$) and neutral species with incomplete octets or vacant orbitals ($\text{BF}_3, \text{AlCl}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{:CH}_2, \text{:CCl}_2$).
• **Nucleophiles ($\text{Nu}^-$)**: Electron-rich species that donate electron pairs (Lewis bases). Include anions ($\text{OH}^-, \text{CN}^-, \text{X}^-$) and neutral molecules with non-bonding lone pairs ($\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{NH}_3, \text{R-OH}$).
• **Ambident Nucleophiles**: Contain two different nucleophilic donor atoms: $\text{CN}^-$ (attacks via $\text{C} \to$ Nitrile; via $\text{N} \to$ Isonitrile); $\text{NO}_2^-$ (attacks via $\text{O} \to$ Alkyl Nitrite; via $\text{N} \to$ Nitroalkane).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Fundamental Organic Reaction Mechanisms
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Fundamental Organic Reaction Mechanisms
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ORGANIC REACTION TYPES

1. Substitution (S): Replacement of an atom/group (S_N1, S_N2, S_EAr)
2. Addition (A): Multiple bond opens to add reagent across π-system (A_E, A_N)
3. Elimination (E): Removal of atoms from adjacent carbons to form π-bond (E1, E2, E1cB)
4. Rearrangement: Intramolecular migration of atoms/groups yielding constitutional isomers
conceptBreakdown.content:
Organic transformations fall into four major mechanistic pathways:
1. **Substitution ($S$)**: Nucleophilic ($S_N1, S_N2$), Electrophilic ($S_E\text{Ar}$), or Free Radical ($S_R$).
2. **Addition ($A$)**: Electrophilic addition to alkenes/alkynes ($A_E$) or Nucleophilic addition to carbonyls ($A_N$).
3. **Elimination ($E$)**: Dehydrohalogenation or dehydration forming alkenes ($E1, E2, E1\text{cB}$).
4. **Rearrangement**: Intramolecular migration (*carbocation shifts, Pinacol-Pinacolone, Beckmann*).

quickRevision: Carbenes (:CH₂, :CCl₂) and BF₃ are neutral electrophiles.
Cyanide (CN⁻) and Nitrite (NO₂⁻) are ambident nucleophiles.
Addition across double bonds is typically electrophilic (A_E).
Addition to carbonyls (>C=O) is typically nucleophilic (A_N).
